externalGates.name: Players hold saves worth keeping
externalGates.notes: Releases the secondary tier. Until real players hold saved runs, discarding a save on a schema bump costs nothing worth migrating.

milestones.name: Foundations and launch
milestones.goal: Get the game as it stands onto a public URL, so every later change ships somewhere real.

tasks.description: Create the public GitHub repository and push the existing history
tasks.notes: https://github.com/JasonWarrenUK/urheimat

tasks.description: Deploy the current client-side game to Vercel from the repository
tasks.notes: https://urheimat.vercel.app/

milestones.name: Design spikes
milestones.goal: Answer the open design questions before building on assumptions that may not survive them.

tasks.description: Gameplay-loop spike: interrogate the core premise, victory conditions, action economy and pacing, evaluate the six existing mechanics (Hold, Reform, Teach, Consolidate, Daughter band, Migrate), and define how condition, strain and action-budget states are derived
tasks.notes: Everything is open, including whether eight eras of three actions ending in a reconstruction is the right shape at all. Output is a design decision plus new tasks for whatever it finds wanting.

tasks.description: UI spike: information architecture first, then visual design; defines how the derived states are displayed, and produces concrete mobile and accessibility tasks rather than principles
tasks.notes: Absorbs the former standalone mobile and accessibility objectives. Gated on state derivation because it cannot design the display of states whose derivation is unsettled. The canvas map currently has no keyboard or screen-reader path; that gap must leave this spike as real tasks. After 2DS.1: also designs the display of the new derived states (recognition; settledness and writing as hidden custom categories; leader and generation), the timelapse after band death and what a watched lull shows. After 2DS.3: also designs the notebook's visual design (look, typography, mobile) over 2DS.3's wireframes; the toggle's granularity is settled there. From 6SL.6: also designs how a strand that stands out is shown in prose (the panel is quiet in ordinary times), the warnings each ladder gives and the health and morale lines. Decided in the 2DS.1 spike (docs/spikes/2DS.1-gameplay-loop.md, decisions 2u, 3t, 5d) and the 2DS.3 spike (docs/spikes/2DS.3-notebook-design.md, decision 2a). From 6SL.6: bands now work as many tiles as their numbers need, so the map is large (4SD.19) and this spike designs how it is shown.

tasks.description: Notebook design spike: the structure, toggle behaviour, prose and wireframe-level layout of the scholars' notebook
tasks.notes: Prose only, no totals. Works from the subjects table in the spike log, combined or spread as the design finds best; settles how the believed/true toggle works and how a band that died early reads. Decided in the 2DS.1 spike (docs/spikes/2DS.1-gameplay-loop.md, decisions 2b, 2c, 2e, 2g, 2j).

milestones.name: Persistence
milestones.goal: Runs survive the session and finished runs are kept, attributed to a signed-in player.

tasks.description: Build the MongoDB data layer: runs and scores collections with their document shapes and access helpers
tasks.notes: Document shapes are already declared as RunDocument and ScoreDocument in src/lib/types.ts; the driver and adapter are installed.

tasks.description: Wire Auth.js with a GitHub OAuth app and enforce document ownership in the server routes
tasks.notes: Depends on the deploy for the live callback URL. MongoDB has no row-level security, so ownership checks live in the SvelteKit server routes rather than the database. Also provisions the Atlas cluster the live deploy needs for the OAuth callback URL. Verified live on 2026-09-18: GitHub OAuth round trip writes user, account and session; /api/runs returns 401 anonymous and only the signed-in player's own runs otherwise, excluding another player's run and an ownerless document.

tasks.description: Save and resume a run across sessions and devices
tasks.notes: Saves are version-gated and discarded this phase: deserialiseState returns null when a saved run's schemaVersion differs from SCHEMA_VERSION (src/lib/sim/serialise.ts), so save/resume does not wait on the tasks that change GameState's shape. Forward migration of saved runs lives in a secondary tier, released once players hold saves worth keeping. Scope line set when 3PL.2 landed: that task shipped the auth mechanism, the requirePlayerId ownership guard and GET /api/runs. The save POST, the delete route and the client-side resume wiring all belong here.

tasks.description: Archive of finished runs: unranked records (people, seed, how it ended), each able to rebuild its notebook on demand
tasks.notes: Replaces the leaderboard; there is no score to rank by. ScoreDocument loses total and max, a breaking change to a stored document shape. The archive keeps what is needed to rebuild the notebook, not its text. Sharing an archived notebook is out of scope for this phase. Decided in the 2DS.3 spike (docs/spikes/2DS.3-notebook-design.md, decisions 7a, 7b, 7c). Ships with integration tests for the archive helpers, which replace recordScore.

tasks.description: Wire integration tests for the runs access helpers in src/lib/server/, against the compose.yaml instance from 3PL.1 (or mongodb-memory-server if that proves less friction in CI)
tasks.notes: The data layer ships with pure-function tests only; the connection and CRUD helpers are exercised by a manual smoke test, not committed. This closes that gap before 3PL.3 builds save/resume on top of them.

milestones.name: Simulation depth
milestones.goal: Deepen the drift model and inter-culture dynamics so reconstruction has something harder to work on.

tasks.description: Remove the aggregate strain count; the per-custom fit line is all that remains
tasks.notes: Strain is per custom only, and pressures are simply the situations of the turn. Decided in the 2DS.1 spike (docs/spikes/2DS.1-gameplay-loop.md, decisions 5b).

tasks.description: Semantic drift: place feature values on a similarity graph so drift favours near neighbours
tasks.notes: Sky to Storm should be likelier than Sky to Sea. This also lets the scholars reconstruct a plausible intermediate rather than only a right or wrong value. Built in the pilot: three tag kinds (about, readings as full grids, material as transitions), a vocabulary with path families and an opposites list, lenses mirroring the tag schema with one default lens, value ids, five named affinity levels, staged customs with material flow, part predicates enforced as dormant parts, and the corpus-fit evidence script. Treatment of the dead was rebuilt as three stages of six parts and fully tagged.

tasks.description: Prestige asymmetry: borrowing flows down the prestige gradient rather than symmetrically by contact weight
tasks.notes: Creates the areal-feature trap: unrelated neighbours converging because they all copied the same prosperous culture. Prestige reads the standing strand of condition (6SL.20). Decided in the 2DS.1 spike (docs/spikes/2DS.1-gameplay-loop.md, decisions 5e).

tasks.description: Second founding stock: seed two unrelated ancestral cultures at game start
tasks.notes: The player's line still descends from one stock; the second exists to contaminate the record and to make a mistaken origin possible (spike decision 2i). From 4SD.16: marriage/people: other (a partner from another founding stock) becomes satisfiable here.

tasks.description: Substrate inheritance: dying and displaced cultures leave traces in whoever succeeds them
tasks.notes: Needs a second lineage to inherit from, so it follows the second founding stock. Traces may be unrelated traditions or mutated sibling ones.

tasks.description: Taboo and deliberate archaism: sanctify a custom against drift, or revive one already lost
tasks.notes: Decides whether sanctifying exists and how it costs; the spike log holds a think-through of its impact under a loop with no random drift. Revival draws on the spirit's complete memory against the band's fading one. Decided in the 2DS.1 spike (docs/spikes/2DS.1-gameplay-loop.md, decisions 4f, 1g).

tasks.description: Inter-culture relations: raids, conquest and absorption, and peaceful relations (trade, alliance, marriage), some player-started
tasks.notes: Possible actions are defined by both parties' custom and development, and evolve with them. Absorption ends the player's run when the lineage no longer holds authority; the rule for which band absorbs which must be transparent, and an equal merger needs a ruling. Decided in the 2DS.1 spike (docs/spikes/2DS.1-gameplay-loop.md, decisions 2t, 4j, 4l). From 6SL.6: real trade replaces the gift and beg stand-ins in 6SL.21's surplus storylets, and absorption becomes the outcome of 6SL.19's small-and-shunned route, which ends in extinction until it exists.

tasks.description: Expand the corpus: more customs, more parts per custom, more values per part
tasks.notes: Content work. Depends on the tagging task because new values are written with their ids, tags, readings, material and affinities as they are added; the funeral pilot set the shape (atomic parts, stages, rule-values). From 4SD.16: how gender is assigned (birth, rite, choice); the hero's passage as a reading family; a grain kind for substance so a harvest feast can shadow it. From 6SL.6: dividing livelihood labour by the kinds a band recognises is 4SD.18's, which assumes recognised kinds as the vocabulary gender assignment settles.

tasks.description: Territory as a gated custom: every band starts as a wandering point and keeps a seat; settling, expanding and abandoning land
tasks.notes: A band's seat is the tile it holds. Food now comes from the tiles its range works (6SL.6: itinerant sources afresh each step, fields held, tiles a shared commons), so spike decision 3k's single seat no longer holds for food; claims, ownership and crowding between bands are decided here, after 4SD.20's design spike on how bands share tiles. Settle and expand can be player-started; abandoning land arises from situations (environment, raids by non-settled bands). Move costs by settledness are tuned here. Decided in the 2DS.1 spike (docs/spikes/2DS.1-gameplay-loop.md, decisions 3k, 3v, 4h, 4j). From the 4SD.4 pilot: custom-level absence (a band without a given custom) shares this gated mechanism. From 6SL.3: settledness as a pull on custom, read from band history, is defined here. From 6SL.6: the food buffer's cap depends on lifestyle, since a granary implies a settled band; 6SL.6 stands in a counter of steps spent on the current seat (a move resets it), so replace that counter with the real settledness custom here and revisit the cap curve.

tasks.description: Writing as a gated custom in grades, from tallies to full record
tasks.notes: A settled band reaches it sooner. Each grade fixes more of what the band knows into the record; early writing does not mean a full record. Decided in the 2DS.1 spike (docs/spikes/2DS.1-gameplay-loop.md, decisions 2n, 3j). From the 6SL.12 split: the storylets for writing's first grade are authored here, with the custom.

tasks.description: Dated knowledge between every pair of bands, with recognition by graded resemblance
tasks.notes: What each band knows of every other and when it learnt it. A close match to a dated record is taken for the same people, a partial match for kin, a poor match for strangers; a better match across all records corrects an earlier identification. Provenance must be robust enough for the scholars to spot paradoxes and the truth toggle to explain them. Decided in the 2DS.1 spike (docs/spikes/2DS.1-gameplay-loop.md, decisions 2k, 2s, 2v, 2w).

tasks.description: Tag material traces value by value across the corpus, without presuming the corpus's customs are valid categories: a custom such as the sacred drink may describe nothing real, and the pass should say so rather than tag around it
tasks.notes: Some values of a custom leave remains and others do not; the category level is too coarse. Decided in the 2DS.1 spike (docs/spikes/2DS.1-gameplay-loop.md, decisions 2l). From the 4SD.4 pilot: traces become a fourth tag kind on values (what a practice leaves in the ground); deictic rules such as facing the first homeland need referents from band history (origin tile, split tile, seat before the last move), which Culture does not yet keep. The corpus's customs are authored categories, not findings. The scholars reconstruct only categories the evidence supports; a custom that turns out to be an artefact of the authoring rather than of any people is flagged for removal or redefinition in 4SD.16.

tasks.description: Record history: each band's custom changes and positions, step by step, in the history 6SL.6 starts
tasks.notes: Today only current state is stored, so neither book can tell customs over time, routes or turning points. Feeds the true book and, through the evidence model, the scholars' book. From the 2DS.3 spike (docs/spikes/2DS.3-notebook-design.md, decisions 1e, 1f). From 6SL.6: one history store. 6SL.6 keeps the per-step strand snapshots on each band and the structured events (kind, band, step, reason) on the game state; this task extends both with custom changes and positions rather than building a second structure.

tasks.description: Tag the corpus: readings, meaning tags, material and named affinity levels for the remaining 15 customs, in recursive loops
tasks.notes: One custom per round, top-down: contract, ids, contract check, then full reading grids per value with cells struck deliberately. Carries the sacred-substance decisions (contract B: a sacred substance taken in the rite; custom id substance), holy-place as a cross-custom reading (needs a predicate for when that custom is absent), the guest render branch becoming a predicate, restating legacy affinity tables in named levels, and the lens sweep via scripts/evidence/corpus-fit.ts, from which Jason picks the default lens values. Decided in the 4SD.4 pilot.

tasks.description: Band-held belief: a band holds one reading of each practice, and belief can drift apart from practice
tasks.notes: Reinterpretation: a people keeps boat burial while its reason slides from the body being unclean to the spirit needing the afterlife. Practice leaves material traces; belief leaves none, so the scholars can recover the boat and get the reason wrong. A reading's when-condition limits which readings a band can hold. Decided in the 4SD.4 pilot.

tasks.description: Labour by recognised kinds: each livelihood source's worked-by becomes a set of the kinds the band recognises, replacing the men, the women and all together
tasks.notes: The current values hard-code two genders. The change reaches the labour tags that pull descent and residence (PULLS in slots.ts), the cross-custom constraint on sex nouns (6SL.5), how gender is assigned (4SD.10) and the unrecognised condition. Replaces and deletes the interim labour rule in 6SL.6's food model. Decided in the 6SL.6 log (docs/spikes/6SL.6-condition-strands-log.md).

tasks.description: Larger map: a map large enough for bands to need many tiles
tasks.notes: With realistic densities a forager band of 150 works about five tiles of 100 square kilometres, so the 9 by 7 map cannot hold the ten bands the cap allows. Touches genMap (its seeded draws, so every seeded result and the baselines move), startTiles, contact (the distance bands), the cap on live bands, the world map display and the evidence scripts. Decided in the 6SL.6 log (docs/spikes/6SL.6-condition-strands-log.md, Range).

tasks.description: Tile range: how range interacts with moves, splits, crowding, standing, conflict and territory, including a design spike on how bands share tiles
tasks.notes: 6SL.6 builds range scoped to food and livelihood: tiles are a shared commons and nothing is claimed. This task explores how range meets the other mechanisms: where a move or a daughter band can go and why, the open-land and hunger split avenues, crowding as a death route (6SL.19), neighbours' regard for a band that wears shared land (6SL.20), raids and absorption (6SL.17, 4SD.9) and territory (4SD.11). It opens with a design spike on how bands share tiles (commons, exclusive claims, persistent claims), which 4SD.11 follows. Decided in the 6SL.6 log (docs/spikes/6SL.6-condition-strands-log.md, Range).

milestones.name: Reconstruction
milestones.goal: Make the scholars fallible in ways that reward how the player played, not just what survived.

tasks.description: The evidence model: what the scholars can draw on, band by band
tasks.notes: The scholars know the end state perfectly and cannot converse with anyone. For a vanished band they have material remains, others' writing about it, its own writing and tales among other peoples. The chronicle is one record among several. The evidence kinds widen beyond those four; undecided candidates are listed in the 2DS.3 log. Decided in the 2DS.1 spike (docs/spikes/2DS.1-gameplay-loop.md, decisions 2o, 2p, 2q) and the 2DS.3 spike (docs/spikes/2DS.3-notebook-design.md, decisions 5a, 5b).

tasks.description: Attestation derived from the evidence model, band by band and value by value, never from a random roll
tasks.notes: A band that kept carved stones, held a long stable period or sat in broad contact leaves more for the scholars. Decided in the 2DS.1 spike (docs/spikes/2DS.1-gameplay-loop.md, decisions 2q).

tasks.description: Deeper scholar model: weighted evidence, competing hypotheses and sub-grouping rather than flat comparison
The notebook accounts for the second stock: contamination misleads, and a band can be given the wrong origin entirely
tasks.notes: False unity across the two stocks, and false separation within one, are both readings the scholars can reach. Soft-linked to the scholar model, which it should reflect but need not wait for.

tasks.description: Notebook shell: two books (the scholars' and the true), a whole-book switch on every page, chapters and navigation
tasks.notes: Opens on the scholars' side; a flip lands on the other book's contents page. Introduction followed by a UI link to your line's trail of chapters; contents with world summaries first, then bands as a family tree; chapter pages link to contents, parent and daughters and every band named in the prose. Prose only, no totals. Deterministic from the stored run so an archived notebook can be rebuilt. Decided in the 2DS.3 spike (docs/spikes/2DS.3-notebook-design.md, decisions 3a, 3d, 3e, 4b to 4d, 6a to 6f, 7b).

tasks.description: The scholars' book: one named scholar's account, over the peoples and family tree the scholars believe in
tasks.notes: The scholar comes from a small authored cast; their biases tip close calls only. Sources are cited. Rival schools are the other cast members, cited by name. A band can be given a wrong origin entirely. A vanished band's chapter is shorter and hedged by evidence kind; a band with no evidence has no chapter. Decided in the 2DS.1 spike (2i) and the 2DS.3 spike (docs/spikes/2DS.3-notebook-design.md, decisions 1d, 3b, 3f to 3j, 5a, 5c).

tasks.description: The true book: an omniscient history of every band, in a voice distinct from the scholar's
tasks.notes: Recounts the whole run so the player is reminded of what happened. Band chapters are a chronological narrative followed by short thematic sections. Remarks on the scholars' errors in its own voice; carries the silences. Decided in the 2DS.3 spike (docs/spikes/2DS.3-notebook-design.md, decisions 1e, 1f, 3c, 3i, 4e, 6e).

tasks.description: Partial credit in reconstruction: a near verdict with partial points when the scholars land on a similar value
tasks.notes: Uses the similarity tables from 4SD.4. Keep it out of the scholars' agreement test: near matches must not count as agreement, since values tied to the same land sit close together. Decided in the 4SD.4 pilot.

milestones.name: The situation loop
milestones.goal: Replace the order menu with situations and answers, so that every change in a band's customs is something somebody saw happen.

tasks.description: World step and leaders: a fixed 25-year step for every band, leaders with a child at 18 and death between 36 and 75, family ages tracked
tasks.notes: Succession passes to the nearest adult descendant; the age range guarantees one exists. A more robust descent and inheritance system is a later phase. Decided in the 2DS.1 spike (docs/spikes/2DS.1-gameplay-loop.md, decisions 3b, 3c, 3q).

tasks.description: Remove the order menu and the action budget: an era becomes situations, answers, step
tasks.notes: Decided in the 2DS.1 spike (docs/spikes/2DS.1-gameplay-loop.md, decisions 3l, 3o).

tasks.description: Layer 1 pressures: surface the land's and neighbours' pull on a custom as a situation with written answers, replacing random drift for all bands
tasks.notes: "Let it lie" is the pull's diegetic outcome: the land and a neighbour win, a memory fizzles. A value the band once held and lost is weighted down unless a neighbour practises it or the land favours it. Decided in the 2DS.1 spike (docs/spikes/2DS.1-gameplay-loop.md, decisions 3m, 3w, 4a, 4e, 4m). Built here: a pull per source (the land, each neighbour in contact, memory, past landscapes, livelihood on descent through the corpus PULLS table, absence as a per-part empty affinity), pulls building on the band to a hold, a cap of three a step, sets changing by add, drop or swap, a lens per cause of change (scarcity and upheaval) for the third course, AI bands taking the let-it-lie outcome until 6SL.7. Log: docs/spikes/6SL.3-pressures-log.md. Moved out: a marriage rule with no qualifying band in reach to 6SL.17, settledness as a pull to 4SD.11, the food channel's prosperity tuning to 6SL.6.

tasks.description: Answer effects: the one-turn keep and reform from any source; a reform can bite back with a follow-up situation
tasks.notes: Answers are derived from many sources: the storylet, combinations of existing customs, ancestral customs, things learnt from neighbours, things provoked by the environment. Decided in the 2DS.1 spike (docs/spikes/2DS.1-gameplay-loop.md, decisions 3l, 4a, 4b, 4d). From 4SD.16: an answer may add, drop or swap a member of a set-valued part. From 6SL.6: condition gained is the generic strand consequence that 6SL.6 supplies; a cautious answer names the strand it improves, and a reform answer can name the strands it costs.

tasks.description: Prerequisite structure and storylet engine: conditions on world and band state, firing, answers and consequences
tasks.notes: One structure gates storylets, writing and territory alike. Decided in the 2DS.1 spike (docs/spikes/2DS.1-gameplay-loop.md, decisions 3a, 3r). From the 4SD.4 pilot: conditions query tags with scope (a custom that releases from an oath), and a band may lack a custom altogether, modelled as custom-level absence rather than a none value. From 4SD.16: the sex nouns other customs use (youth's rites, place's access, livelihood's labour, marriage's plural, the powers' address readings) must stay consistent with the gender custom's recognised kinds: a cross-custom constraint.

tasks.description: Condition core: a hidden headcount with size tiers, food as yield against numbers with a surplus buffer, health and morale as strands, the generic strand vocabulary and the ladder engine; replaces prosperity
tasks.notes: Split into five tasks (6SL.6, 6SL.10, 6SL.19, 6SL.20, 6SL.21); the reasoning behind each item below is in docs/spikes/6SL.6-condition-strands-log.md. Replaces the former 4SD.1. No numbers shown, open to reconsideration. King of Dragon Pass is the example, analysed in the 2DS.1 spike log. Decided in the 2DS.1 spike (docs/spikes/2DS.1-gameplay-loop.md, decisions 5a, 5e, 5f). Scope: numbers as a hidden headcount with named size tiers; food as heads fed against numbers (a density per square kilometre and heads fed per worker for each source, a minimum team, the land's affinity and richness, tile pools drawn down and regrown), with a surplus buffer capped by a keeps field on each livelihood value and by a counter of steps on the current seat that stands in for settledness; health and morale, always present; the generic strand consequence and condition with named targets, replacing the prosperity forms, with every existing answer remapped to a strand for review; the generic ladder engine (strength gates surfacing, refusals set the tier, a forced top tier, combined situations as authored storylets outside the cap) with one example route, famine, that 6SL.19 replaces; whole-band move costs (buffer cut, seat counter reset); per-step strand snapshots for every band and structured events beside the chronicle; a prose line when a strand stands out; interim rules for death (headcount zero) and AI splits, each labelled for deletion by 6SL.19 and 6SL.10; schema bumps with older saves discarded (3PL.3). From 6SL.3: with only food strain feeding prosperity the base game drifts upward (near the cap by era 6); tune the food strand here. 4SD.11 soft-depends on this task: if it lands first, read real settledness and build no seat counter. Food is in heads fed, set against the headcount: a ceiling per source is a base figure times the terrain affinity weight times one plus richness, hands come from the working band split by recognised kind, and labour uses an interim rule (the men and the women draw on their own kind, all-together sources on every recognised kind, other kinds on all-together sources only) that 4SD.18 replaces. Range: a band works as many tiles as its numbers need (densities per square kilometre, a tile of 100): itinerant sources pick tiles afresh each step within reach 2, the hoe and the plough hold fields within reach 1, and tiles are a shared commons with nothing claimed. Figures cite research or are marked assumptions. A much bigger map (4SD.19) and how range meets the other mechanisms (4SD.20) follow this task.

tasks.description: Scripted answers for AI bands, shaped by conservatism and drive, reported in the chronicle
tasks.notes: Decided in the 2DS.1 spike (docs/spikes/2DS.1-gameplay-loop.md, decisions 4k). From 6SL.6: the scripts also answer the death, split and surplus ladder situations; until then an AI band resolves each by its let-it-lie outcome.

tasks.description: Weather and lulls: situation count by pressure, fine-weather opportunities, watched steps with chronicle lines
tasks.notes: Pressure behaves like weather, with peaks and lulls and no climb towards the end. Decided in the 2DS.1 spike (docs/spikes/2DS.1-gameplay-loop.md, decisions 3i, 3p, 3t).

tasks.description: Band memory: what the people remember of each custom's past fades by generation and breaks at a split, while the spirit's view stays complete
tasks.notes: Ancestral answers draw on what the band remembers. The spirit is a frame only, never named in the game. Decided in the 2DS.1 spike (docs/spikes/2DS.1-gameplay-loop.md, decisions 1d, 1e, 1g, 1h).

tasks.description: Split ladders: a daughter band as an outcome of pressure (hunger, quarrel) or opportunity (open land), with the player choosing which branch to follow
tasks.notes: The daughter's condition is derived from the parent's condition, the narrative reason for the split and the land it spawns on. Decided in the 2DS.1 spike (docs/spikes/2DS.1-gameplay-loop.md, decisions 2d, 4g) and the 6SL.6 log (docs/spikes/6SL.6-condition-strands-log.md). Routes are data on 6SL.6's ladder engine: hunger, quarrel and open land, with the numbers tier as one more input; a standing avenue waits for the leaders' internal reputation strand. A split arrives as a situation whose acceptance and refusal both carry pros and cons; refusing while the pressure remains climbs to higher-stakes storylets, live split pulls combine into one situation, and a forced split at the top tier is rare. Heads are shared by reason: hunger sends out those the land cannot feed, a quarrel a faction, open land a small party; the daughter starts with that reason's health and morale. Deletes 6SL.6's interim AI split roll. The cause of the original scattering is either this task's first split resolved by consent at era 0 or 6SL.14's intro; 6SL.6 starts the bands from a share of the home tile's capacity and names no cause.

tasks.description: Moves: forced by events, or player-started with diegetic justification or a consequence
tasks.notes: In the early game a move is the only act the player can start unprompted. Decided in the 2DS.1 spike (docs/spikes/2DS.1-gameplay-loop.md, decisions 3s, 4i). From 6SL.6: this task supplies the reason for a move (forced or chosen), which the morale and head costs of a move read; 6SL.6 already cuts the food buffer and resets the seat counter on every whole-band move.

tasks.description: Storylet corpus, first batch: pressure-agnostic storylets on state the engine already exposes (leaders, succession, the land, contact, the customs a band holds, events, history), enough for a medium run
tasks.notes: Authored with cooldowns and once flags doing 6SL.8's job of capping situations per step until weather lands. Writing's first grade belongs to 4SD.12; pressure and bite-back storylets to the second batch. Decided in the 2DS.1 spike (docs/spikes/2DS.1-gameplay-loop.md, decision 3a).

tasks.description: Run ending: history arrives once written record begins, a sky-clock fallback with a power from beyond when writing has stalled, the player may stop, and a timelapse of the world to the notebook
tasks.notes: The fallback fires only if history has not arrived after a long time and there has been no recent progress towards it. A run is medium to long: fifteen turns or more. Decided in the 2DS.1 spike (docs/spikes/2DS.1-gameplay-loop.md, decisions 2t, 2u, 3j, 3u).

tasks.description: Intro and framing rewrite: no scholars, no rules, no goal; the spirit unnamed
tasks.notes: The player sees no reference to the notebook during play, so the chronicle line "Your testimony ends here" (engine.ts:483) goes too. Decided in the 2DS.1 spike (docs/spikes/2DS.1-gameplay-loop.md, decisions 1c, 1h, 2r). From 6SL.6: the cause of the scattering (the pressure that drove the original band apart) is settled here or in 6SL.10, as the first split resolved by consent; the condition core starts the six bands from a share of the home tile's capacity and names no cause.

tasks.description: Derive the new displayed states: recognition, settledness and writing as hidden custom categories, leader and generation
tasks.notes: Hidden custom categories are invisible until active. Display itself belongs to 2DS.2. Decided in the 2DS.1 spike (docs/spikes/2DS.1-gameplay-loop.md, decisions 5d).

tasks.description: Family opinion as a storylet trigger
tasks.notes: The family is voiceless at first. Decided in the 2DS.1 spike (docs/spikes/2DS.1-gameplay-loop.md, decisions 5g).

tasks.description: Cross-band relationships: warfare (internal versus external) as band state, raids and feuds between bands, and killings between bands
tasks.notes: From 6SL.6: feuds, raids and killings between bands move standing (6SL.20) and numbers. From 4SD.16: residence is pulled by whether a band's warfare is internal or external (Ember and Ember 1971); rule/source: war and justice/remedy: feud are the interim tag signals. A chief answering for a killer belongs to killings between bands and was dropped from justice/answerer until this exists. Marriage's partner rules resolve against the band tree and contact here. From 6SL.3: a marriage rule with no qualifying band in reach is pressure; raise it here once kin distance and reach exist (placeholder threshold two splits).

tasks.description: Storylet corpus, second batch: storylets that answer layer 1 pressures, and reform bite-back (a reform provoking its own situation next step)
tasks.notes: Split out of 6SL.12 because bite-back needs 6SL.4's reform effects and pressure storylets need 6SL.3; the first batch is pressure-agnostic. Decided in the 2DS.1 spike (docs/spikes/2DS.1-gameplay-loop.md, decisions 3a, 4b).

tasks.description: Death ladders: famine, attrition, starved and shunned, and small and shunned, each a ladder of situations ending in the band's end
tasks.notes: Four routes written as data on 6SL.6's ladder engine: famine (adequacy below need once the buffer is spent), attrition (numbers below what keeps a band going), starved and shunned (food with standing) and small and shunned (numbers with standing). Every answer carries pros and cons; refusing while the strands stay low climbs the tiers, the top tier ends the band, and live pulls combine into one situation. Deletes 6SL.6's interim death rule and emits structured events for the notebook. Sudden deaths (raid, plague, massacre) are a later task. Small and shunned ends in extinction until 4SD.9 gives it absorption. Decided in the 6SL.6 log (docs/spikes/6SL.6-condition-strands-log.md).

tasks.description: Standing: each band's regard for another, stored per band and moved by storylet answers, relative size, parentage and shared customs
tasks.notes: Stored per band as each other band's regard, read from its dated knowledge (2k, 2s); the aggregate that prestige needs is derived on read. A storylet answer that moves standing always names the bands concerned, and naming none is an error. Size reads the headcount tiers from 6SL.6, parentage the band tree and shared customs bandSimilarity (src/lib/sim/similarity.ts). The leaders' reputation within a band is not standing and is a later strand. 4SD.5 reads this task; 6SL.17's feuds, raids and killings move it. Decided in the 6SL.6 log (docs/spikes/6SL.6-condition-strands-log.md).

tasks.description: Surplus storylets: a surplus building, drawing on the buffer, the buffer nearly spent and the cap reached, with rationing acting on health and morale
tasks.notes: Storylets reading 6SL.6's buffer against its cap and against numbers. Rationing costs health and saves stores; a feast lifts morale and spends them. Gift and beg answers act on a named neighbour in contact (the band's buffer, standing and the neighbour's own buffer) as stand-ins until 4SD.9 gives real trade. Loss of the buffer (stores rot, raids, a sick herd) is a sudden event for a later task. Decided in the 6SL.6 log (docs/spikes/6SL.6-condition-strands-log.md).

tasks.notes: Replaces the discard-on-mismatch in deserialiseState (src/lib/sim/serialise.ts). Decided in the 2026-10-12 roadmap review of M3: 3PL.3 ships version-gated discard so it does not wait on the shape-changing tasks.
